records.csv_project_name: Design Services for Campus Wide Assessment
records.title: Design Services for Campus Wide Assessment
records.project_scope: Campus-wide assessment and feasibility study for converting the University of New Mexico heating infrastructure from steam-based systems to electrified low-temperature hot water solutions. Scope includes comparative concepts for individual building conversions and combined building hubs; routing and siting of plants; interconnections and looped distribution configurations; utility and roadway crossings; resiliency, isolation and valving strategies; evaluation of ties to existing plants or future energy centers; and comparison of electric heat sources such as heat recovery chillers, ambient loop heat pumps, thermal storage, and electric boilers. At building level, the consultant must review records and perform field walkthroughs for identified buildings, classify them into Green/Yellow/Red conversion categories, assess residual steam needs, define domestic hot water strategies, and prepare schematic flow diagrams and control narratives. The assignment also includes load analysis, option comparison, phasing plans, and Class 4/5 opinions of probable cost for campus distribution, building conversions, heat-source equipment, controls integration, and commissioning. The study must address reliability, resiliency, decarbonization, lifecycle value, and constructability while protecting academic, research, and patient-care operations.
